English: Ember Stand
A simple stone platform where sacred embers are kept alight, tended by the faithful to preserve Zoroastrian tradition on the frontier.
Torch Post
A ring of wooden posts with ever-burning torches, marking a growing congregation and providing light and hope to the nomadic faithful.
Fire Pit
A communal pit, lined with stones and clay, where the sacred fire is tended day and night. The fire pit draws both worshippers and wandering clans.
Flame Pavilion
A large tented structure with decorated banners and a raised hearth, allowing for the gathering of priests and the performance of greater rituals.
Priests Room
Partitioned sleeping and study quarters for the Mobeds, the priestly class, enabling the teaching of doctrine and deeper community ties.
Altar Chamber
A semi-permanent structure of mud brick and timber, housing a stone altar for major rites and the preservation of holy relics.
Sanctified Hall
A proper wooden and brick hall, adorned with sacred motifs, where large assemblies and feasts can be held to honor the faith and unify the clans.
Holy Fire Pavilion
A multi-tented complex with a domed shelter for the Atash Bahram, housing the most sacred fire and drawing pilgrims from distant lands.
Blessed Sanctuary
A grand, semi-permanent sanctuary of fired brick, with marble tiles and a rooftop vent for the sacred fire. The sanctuary unites the clans in worship and strengthens the faiths prestige.
Iranian Grand Fire Temple
A monumental stone temple with high domes, gilded altars, and a great hall for all the clans. The eternal flame blazes within, cementing your legacy as a true champion of the faith.
